conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, this is Officer Michael Reed with the IRS Tax Refund Department. May I speak with Jamie Thompson, please?
Yes, this is Jamie. I'm at work, can we make this quick?
Absolutely, Jamie. We're calling because our records show you are eligible for a $3,200 tax refund, but before we can release the funds, we need to confirm some details for IRS compliance.
Wait, a refund? I already filed my taxes, are you sure this is right?
Yes, this is an additional stimulus refund adjustment related to recent IRS tax relief programs. But, to process this, you need to verify your identity and pay a mandatory processing fee.
A fee? I've never heard of that before. Isn't the IRS supposed to just send the money?

Under normal circumstances, yes. However, due to increased fraud, the IRS now requires a one-time $195 verification fee to be paid before issuing any new refunds. If you do not complete this step, your refund will be cancelled and flagged for audit.
I really can't afford to be audited right now, I'm a single mom and things are already stressful. Can't you just take it from the refund?

Unfortunately, IRS policy prohibits deducting fees from refunds. If you fail to pay today, your name will be submitted to our tax compliance unit, and you could face penalties or even a freeze on your bank accounts.
That sounds serious. What do I need to do to avoid this?

You need to send the $195 fee today. We are only authorized to accept payment via instant methods for security reasons. Do you have access to Cash App, Zelle, or can you purchase a Visa prepaid card at a local store?
I guess I could get a Visa gift card on my lunch break. Is that really the only way?
Yes, that's the fastest and only secure IRS-approved method for immediate clearance. If not completed today, your case will be flagged as noncompliant and subject to further legal action.
Okay, okay, I'll go as soon as I drop my daughter at daycare. Then what?
Once you have the Visa gift card, call us back at this number and read out the card number and security code on the back. Only then can your refund be processed and the audit halted.
Can I do it online instead? I really don't have time to run errands today.
No exceptions, Jamie. The IRS requires physical verification for this process. Failure to comply will result in immediate escalation to our enforcement division. We can't delay.
Alright, I'll get the card and call you after work. Please don't flag my account yet.
If you do not call back by 4pm today, we'll have no choice but to initiate a hold on your tax records and notify collections. Do you understand the consequences?
Yes, I understand. I really don't want any trouble.
Good. Remember, any delay will result in forfeiture of your refund and possible legal penalties. Have your card ready and call us as soon as possible. We'll be waiting for your confirmation.
